subject: LexaHealth RFP — commercial commit and surge hedging
messages:

Subject: LexaHealth RFP — commercial questions on commit sizing and surge handling

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the routing controls. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of commercial clarifications so we can include Redwood in the final vendor score:

1) We want a firm annual commit (tokens/month) with an explicit surge mechanism for unpredictable events. Can you outline a construct that protects our unit economics while giving us access to burst capacity without crippling overage exposure?
2) Do you support a capacity escrow (pre-funded pool) that automatically covers overages at a discounted burst rate before invoicing the overage to a standard price?
3) Please provide an example calculation for a quarter with 20% burst above commit and show how true-up/credits would work at invoice time.
4) Any preferred language you recommend for the SOW about rollover, true-up cadence, and breakage?

We'd like to get your response by EOD Friday so we can finalize the commercial scoring. Attaching the commercial section of the RFP for reference (not attached here).

Best,
Jordan

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Patel <j.patel@lexahealth.com>, LexaHealth Procurement <procurement@lexahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-22T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LexaHealth RFP — commercial questions on commit sizing and surge handling

Jordan — great questions. Below is a concise commercial construct tailored to a healthcare SaaS workload (sensitive PII but no PHI in inference):

Executive summary (proposal):
- Annual committed tokens: 120M tokens (10M/month floor) at a base unit price of $0.0009/token.
- Surge escrow (pre-funded pool): Optional pre-funded surge escrow equal to 10% of annual commit (12M tokens). Escrow usage applies a discounted burst rate of $0.00065/token when consumed.
- Standard overage (post-escrow): $0.0015/token. Overage invoices are net of any escrow consumption.
- True-up cadence: Quarterly reconciliation; unused escrow tokens roll forward within the contract year; at year-end remaining escrow may be refunded or applied as credit toward renewal at customer's election.
- Rollover: Monthly unused committed tokens (from the 10M monthly allocation) may carry forward up to a 3-month window (max 30M) to smooth seasonality.

Illustrative calculation (Q3 example):
- Committed quarter tokens (3 months): 30M tokens
- Actual consumption: 36M tokens (20% burst)
- Escrow available at start of quarter: 3.0M tokens (pro-rated from 12M annual escrow)

Stepwise reconciliation:
1) Apply monthly roll-forwards (assume none for this scenario).
2) Consume escrow: 3.0M tokens at $0.00065 = $1,950 credit applied against overage.
3) Remaining burst = 36M - 30M - 3M = 3M tokens billed at standard overage $0.0015 = $4,500.
4) Base committed charge for quarter = 30M * $0.0009 = $27,000.
5) Net quarter invoice = $27,000 + $4,500 = $31,500 (escrow consumed, so no separate escrow invoice).

Example with partial escrow refund option: If Lexa elects not to roll unused escrow at year-end, remaining escrow tokens are refunded at a rate of $0.0005/token.

Additional commercial levers (optional, can be combined):
- Onboarding credit: one-time 200k token credit applied in month 1 for proof-of-concept and prompt tuning.
- Volume discount ladder on committed unit price: 0-120M @ $0.0009; 120M-300M @ $0.0008; 300M+ custom pricing (requires review).
- SLA credit: latency SLA > 99.5% for p95 token latency; failure to meet SLA triggers a service credit applied as% of monthly committed charge (example: 5% credit for p95 breach).

Term language suggestions (SOW snippets):
- "Commit and Escrow": "Customer shall commit to the Annual Committed Tokens. Customer may elect to fund a Surge Escrow at contract start. Escrow tokens are drawn prior to overage invoicing and are priced at the Escrow Burst Rate when consumed."
- "True-Up": "Provider will reconcile consumed tokens vs committed tokens quarterly and invoice net overage. Rolling credits shall not exceed the monthly carry-forward cap stated above."

Attachments: commercial term sheet and a simple calculation workbook (attached).

Next steps: If this construct looks good I can put the term sheet into DocuSign and include the sample calculation workbook. Otherwise I can run a variant with a higher escrow (20%) and different refund mechanics for you to compare.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-22T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: LexaHealth RFP — pricing construct (internal)

Quick internal note before we send the final DocuSign:

- Margin impact: the escrow burst rate at $0.00065 is close to variable cost when quantized on the target hardware. If we do onboarding credit + 10% escrow + the two-tier commit discount ladder, incremental margin compression is ~7-9% on year-one ARR.
- Proposal to preserve margin: tighten the refund at year-end (refund at $0.00035/token) and limit escrow carry-forward to two quarters instead of annual rollover. That lowers long-tail exposure.
- Sales ask: Can we offer a one-time implementation discount of 5% on the first quarter committed charge (not on overage) as a sweetener? That helps close and is easy to show in the SOW.

Marissa — can you confirm revenue recognition constraints if we apply the onboarding credit and 5% implementation discount? Aditya — any technical concerns on supporting the escrow accounting (we already have a pre-paid credit ledger but need to ensure it maps to token consumption in the telemetry)?

Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts

Jordan — thanks for the quick turn. We've reviewed internally and can confirm the construct below as Redwood's recommended commercial path. Key updates are noted from our internal review:

- Annual commit: 120M tokens at $0.0009/token.
- Surge escrow: 12M tokens (10% of annual commit), consumed at $0.00065/token. Escrow pro-rates quarterly (3.0M per quarter).
- Year-end refund: remaining escrow refundable at $0.00035/token (updated from earlier draft).
- Carry-forward: monthly unused committed tokens may carry forward up to 2 months (max 20M at any time).
- One-time credits: onboarding credit of 200k tokens; 5% implementation discount applied to first quarter committed charge.
- True-up cadence: quarterly reconciliation; overage invoiced net of escrow consumption.

We have attached the term sheet and a worked example workbook. If LexaHealth is comfortable, I'll initiate a DocuSign package with these terms and the SOW snippet for rollover/true-up language. Proposed timeline:
- DocuSign out: Tuesday 2026-10-27
- Signature target: 2026-11-03
- Onboarding kickoff: week of 2026-11-08

Please let me know if you want a variant with a 20% escrow (higher protection, marginally higher price) or if you prefer a mechanism where escrow purchases are indexed to a CPI-like metric for long-term contracts.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this one.
